title: 8 10Web Alternatives That Cost Less
summary: 8 10Web alternatives: 7 with a free plan that stays online, 2 with paid plans under its $20 monthly or $120 prepaid price, and the catches.
body_markdown:
**Key takeaways:**


- 10Web has no free plan that stays online. AI Starter costs $20 month to month, and its $10-a-month rate needs a $120 prepay for 12 months.
- Seven of the eight tools below have a free plan that leaves your site online, and WordPress.com and Framer also match or undercut 10Web's paid price.
- Our own Awesomic Studio, at #1, is the exception: $20 a month with no free plan, which ties 10Web month to month and doubles its prepaid rate.
- Hostinger, IONOS and ZipWP advertise lower first-term prices but renew above 10Web's $10 a month, and GoDaddy Airo's Starter undercuts 10Web by a single cent.


10Web's homepage calls it an "Agentic Website Builder." Its AI agents build and redesign a WordPress site, and 10Web hosts the result. That suits you if you want WordPress underneath without setting it up yourself.


Price is the catch, and it's why we judged these 10Web alternatives on cost. Nothing on 10Web stays live for free, the headline $10 a month applies only if you pay $120 for a year up front, and month to month the same plan costs $20.


So on this list, "costs less" has a strict meaning. A tool qualifies if it passes at least one of two tests:


- It has a free plan that keeps a site live.
- It has a custom-domain plan that costs less than 10Web AI Starter on the same billing basis, meaning under $10 a month on yearly billing or under $20 month to month.


Every entry from #2 to #8 passes the first test, and each review says where its paid plan stops beating 10Web. Our own Awesomic Studio sits at #1 for how it builds, not for its price, and its entry opens with the numbers.


We read every price, limit and quoted line on the vendors' own pages on September 11, 2026, so you can judge the best 10Web alternatives on what they cost in year one and after it.


## Why look for 10Web alternatives?


10Web builds on WordPress. Its Redesign, Clone and Figma agents handle the building, WooCommerce covers selling, and its FAQ says you can "Customize it with 10Web editor based on Elementor."


AI Starter, the cheapest plan, covers 1 website, 100 AI credits a month, 10GB of storage, 10,000 monthly visitors and a free custom domain for the first year.


Each of the three AI plans shows two prices. AI Starter is $20 month to month or $10 a month on a prepaid year, which 10Web advertises as "Get 12 months for $120 (regular price $240)." AI Premium runs $30 or $15 for 2 sites, and AI Ultimate $45 or $22.50 for 4 sites.


Four details on 10Web's own pages are worth reading before you pay:


- "Get started for free" generates a site, but full editing needs a 7-day trial of the Pro version with a credit card attached.
- If you don't upgrade before that trial ends, the help center says "your website will be deleted after the trial expires," though it adds that upgrading later can recover it.
- The pricing page promises a "30-day money back guarantee" that "applies until you claim your free domain," while the help center says "10Web does not offer refunds" and the terms say "All payments are final."
- The terms say fees are "charged/automatically renewed at the beginning of each billing cycle without notifications to you."


Both refund lines are 10Web's own words, and the guarantee ends once you claim the free domain, so hold off on the domain until you're sure.


The pricing page and terms also don't say whether a prepaid year renews at $120 or at the $240 "regular price." The terms only promise an email "at least 72 hours prior to your next billing cycle" if fees change, so ask 10Web in writing before your renewal date.


So the real entry price is $120 paid today or $20 every month, and that's the bar each tool below has to clear. 10Web's FAQ also mentions 2-year and 3-year plans at up to 65% off, and its page data prices AI Starter at $7 a month ($252 for 36 months), but its pricing cards offer only monthly and yearly, so those are what we compare against.


## The best 10Web alternatives at a glance


Rows follow the ranking below. The Pricing (from) column shows each tool's lowest verified price, and every row but the first reads $0 because of a free plan.

WordPress.com Keeping WordPress for less Chat-with-AI builder, plugins on paid plans, free plan Free plan shows ads $0 (free plan) ★★★★★


Framer Design-led sites without a prepay AI design agent, Framer domain on free, 1,000 AI credits a month on Basic No WordPress plugins; pages get rebuilt $0 (free plan) ★★★★★


Wix A free site with no card on file No-card free plan, Wix Harmony AI builder, custom code and apps Light costs $17/month yearly $0 (free plan) ★★★★★

Stars rate how well each tool does 10Web's core job for a small site (build it with AI, edit it, host it), and price moves none of them, since the cost table below covers price. All eight do that job, so each starts at five and loses a star only if its own pages admit little or no room to add your own code, something 10Web gets from WordPress.


### 1. Awesomic Studio


**Best for:** Agent-built sites with human backup


**Overview:** Start with the price. Awesomic Studio's Basic plan costs $20 a month, level with 10Web AI Starter month to month and double its prepaid $10, and Studio has no free plan, so it fails both our tests.


What it shares with 10Web is the method. Both are agentic builders:[Awesomic Studio](https://www.awesomic.com/studio/) hands your brief to its coding agents (Codex, Claude Code and OpenCode), which build the site, and Studio then publishes and hosts it.


The difference is what happens when the agents miss. One of our vetted designers or developers, drawn from the top 0.82% of applicants, picks the project up where the agents left it and returns it to you. Studio's FAQ calls that safety net "built in, not an upsell."


There's no WordPress underneath, so no plugins and no WooCommerce, and Studio makes no ecommerce claim.


**Key features:**


- A brief in text, files or links replaces arranging blocks in an editor.
- The agents write the site as real code.
- Built-in hosting puts it live, privately for your team or publicly.
- Export to code or other tools lets you leave later.
- Scheduled automations keep running updates after you close the tab.
- A human takeover covers the briefs the agents get wrong.


**Pricing:** Basic is the $20 plan; Pro costs $200 and Maximum $500 a month, and each fee also caps what the agents can spend in that month. It lists no cost per model or per build, so month one shows how far $20 goes.


**Pros:** Agents that build, publish and host, a vetted human when they miss, exportable code, private review links, work that runs after you log off


**Cons:** $20 a month ties 10Web's month-to-month price rather than beating it, no free plan, no WordPress backend, plugins, WooCommerce or ecommerce claim


**How to start using it:**


1. Write down who the site is for and what a visitor should do next.
2. Add your current pages as links, plus your logo and copy as files.
3. Start on Basic.
4. Check the draft on a private share link and tell the agents what to change.
5. Publish, or ask for a human takeover if the agents keep missing.


**Why it's a good 10Web alternative:** It keeps the agentic approach you picked 10Web for and adds a person when the agents miss. You give up WordPress and its plugins, so check that your site needs neither.


**Final verdict:** Choose Studio for the build and the human backup, not to save money; a site that depends on WordPress plugins belongs on WordPress, via 10Web or WordPress.com.

### 2. WordPress.com


**Overview:** WordPress.com is Automattic's hosted WordPress, sold under the line "WordPress, done right," and the same CMS family as 10Web.


Leaving 10Web for it is a WordPress-to-WordPress move, so WordPress's own export and import tools can carry your content across.


**Key features:**


- A guided builder to "create and launch a WordPress.com website in minutes by chatting with AI"
- Any of "over 60,000 plugins" on every paid plan, or one you upload yourself
- A free plan to rebuild and check your site on before paying


**Pricing:** On yearly billing, Personal is $4 a month for year one, and after that it renews at $8 or $10 a month (WordPress.com's page showed both figures on September 11, 2026), still billed every 12 months. Paying month to month costs $9, without the free first-year domain, and the free plan carries ads.


**Pros:** The same WordPress you use on 10Web, plugins from the cheapest paid plan, a free plan with a live site


**Cons:** Ads on the free plan, a year-two renewal of $8 to $10 a month, at or under 10Web's prepaid $10, every plugin you add still yours to vet


**Why it's a good 10Web alternative:** Both tests pass here: $9 month to month beats 10Web's $20, and $4 beats $10 in year one, with the renewal landing at or under 10Web's rate.


**Final verdict:** The lowest-effort move if you want to keep WordPress and pay less, especially in year one.


### 3. Framer


**Overview:** Framer's homepage presents it as an "AI design agent" that takes a site "from idea to launch." It suits sites where the look carries the message.


Framer isn't WordPress, so your WordPress plugins stay behind. Its homepage shows an agent importing WordPress blog posts into Framer's CMS, but plan to rebuild the pages.


**Key features:**


- A free plan that stays published on a Framer domain, which Framer calls "ideal for non-commercial use"
- 500 AI credits "to try" on Free, then 1,000 a month on Basic
- Custom code, code components and a plugin marketplace of its own


**Pricing:** Basic runs $15 if you pay monthly, without the complimentary domain, or $10 a month on a yearly plan that includes one. That ties 10Web's prepaid $10 and beats its $20 monthly price.


**Pros:** $5 a month under 10Web when you pay monthly, no year to prepay on Basic, a fresh AI credit allowance every month


**Cons:** No WordPress plugins, pages to rebuild, only a tie with 10Web on yearly billing


**Why it made this list:** It passes both tests, with a free plan to try it on and a monthly Basic plan that still undercuts 10Web.


**Final verdict:** Pick Framer when design matters more than WordPress plugins, and compare the[Framer alternatives](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/framer-alternatives) before you commit to a rebuild.


### 4. Wix


**Overview:** Wix pitches Wix Harmony as "where you create a site that means business," and its free plan starts with "No credit card required."


The free site lives on a username.wixsite.com address and shows Wix ads, which is fine for testing and weak for a business card.


**Key features:**


- Wix Harmony, its AI website builder
- A drag-and-drop editor, free plan included
- Custom code and the Wix App Market for extras


**Pricing:** Light is $17 a month on a yearly subscription paid in full, $7 more than 10Web's prepaid rate. Taxes come on top, set by your billing address.


**Pros:** No card needed to start, a free site that stays live, room for your own code and apps


**Cons:** Wix ads on the free plan, a full year paid up front for the $17 rate, no custom domain until you upgrade


**Where it fits:** It passes the free-plan test only. Once you pay, Light costs more than 10Web does on a prepaid year.


**Final verdict:** A good home for a free site that can wait a while for a paid plan.


### 5. Durable


**Overview:** Durable's homepage headline is "The complete AI business builder," followed by "Get online in 30 seconds." Both are its own marketing lines, and we didn't time the 30 seconds.


Its free plan keeps a site live on a *.durable.site subdomain, and paid plans add a free custom domain.


**Key features:**


- A Blog Writer agent: 2 posts on free, then 10 a month on Launch
- A free custom domain on every paid plan
- A built-in CRM with AI replies to up to 20 leads on Launch


**Pricing:** Launch is $22 a month billed yearly or $25 month to month. That's $12 a month more than 10Web's prepaid rate and $5 more than its monthly one.


**Pros:** A live free site, posts that keep coming after launch, calendar-synced bookings on Launch


**Cons:** Launch costs more than 10Web on either billing basis, no "extensive options for HTML customization," per Durable's FAQ, though Launch lists custom code, a durable.site address on the free plan


**What it does differently:** Durable's agents keep working after launch, with 10 blog posts and 20 AI lead replies a month on Launch.


**Final verdict:** Good for a service business that wants a free site today and hands-off posting later.


### 6. Strikingly


**Overview:** Strikingly's pitch is "Make a website in minutes," and its AI site builder drafts the first version for you.


The free plan allows unlimited sites on a strikingly.com subdomain, and each can sell one product at a 5% fee.


**Key features:**


- An AI site builder that drafts a full site, on up to 5 free sites
- A drag-and-drop mode inside sections, free plan included
- Custom code embeds and up to 100 pages per site on Pro


**Pricing:** Pro costs $16 a month billed yearly and adds a custom domain. That's $6 a month more than 10Web's prepaid AI Starter.


**Pros:** Several free sites (unlimited on its pricing page, 5 per its AI help article), one product on sale without paying for a plan, room for your own code on Pro


**Cons:** A custom domain needs Pro, Pro costs more than 10Web on yearly billing, a 5% fee on free-plan sales


**Why it earns a spot:** Its free plan passes our first test, and free users get the same drag-and-drop mode as paying ones.


**Final verdict:** Useful for trying several site ideas before any of them costs you money.


### 7. Jimdo


**Overview:** Jimdo's homepage reads "Start your website. Get found. Get booked. Get paid." and promises "A website built with AI."


Its free plan, on a .jimdosite.com subdomain, comes with the line "No credit card. Free forever."


**Key features:**


- An AI-built first version of the site
- A booking tool, payment links and invoices beside the site
- Prices quoted with VAT already included


**Pricing:** Start costs $11 a month with your own domain, and Jimdo notes that "Prices apply for a 12-month contract term" and include VAT. That's $1 a month more than 10Web's prepaid rate.


**Pros:** No card to start, bookings and invoices in the same account, no ads from the Start plan up


**Cons:** Start costs $1 more than 10Web prepaid, no custom code or embed codes in its builder, a .jimdosite.com address on free


**Its real strength:** A free site with no end date, the opposite of 10Web's 7-day card trial.


**Final verdict:** Close to 10Web's price once you pay, and free until you do.


### 8. SITE123


**Overview:** SITE123 opens with "Create a Free Website Today!" and an AI chat that builds your first draft from a "Describe your idea" prompt.


Its promise is that "Every SITE123 website is free to use indefinitely," on a SITE123 subdomain.


**Key features:**


- An AI chat that turns your description into a draft
- Plugins and custom code, added from one menu in the editor
- A custom domain on the Premium plan


**Pricing:** Premium, the plan that connects your own domain, shows $12.80 a month on SITE123's pricing card, which names no billing term, while the FAQ on the same page says "as low as $10.8 per month (annual plan, paid up front)." That's 80 cents to $2.80 a month above 10Web's prepaid $10.


**Pros:** Free indefinitely, a chat-built first draft, a 14-day money-back guarantee on Premium


**Cons:** Two different Premium prices on its own pages, at least 80 cents a month above 10Web, a subdomain on the free plan


**Why we included it:** It passes the free-plan test, and you can describe the site instead of designing it.


**Final verdict:** A simple, free start for a first site, as long as you check which Premium price you'll pay before upgrading.

## How much do 10Web alternatives cost?


Here's every entry set against 10Web AI Starter on both tests, using each vendor's own prices from September 11, 2026. Test (a) asks for a free plan with a live site, and test (b) for a cheaper custom-domain plan on the same billing basis.


Tool Free plan with a live site Cheapest paid plan Against 10Web ($10 yearly, $20 monthly) Tests passed

Awesomic Studio No Basic, $20/month Ties the monthly price, double the prepaid one Neither

Framer Yes, on a Framer domain Basic, $10/month yearly or $15 month to month Ties yearly, $5 cheaper monthly (a) and (b)

Seven of the eight pass the free-plan test and two also pass the price test, so a free plan is where most of the saving sits. Once you pay, Jimdo sits $1 above 10Web's prepaid $10 and SITE123 80 cents to $2.80 above it, while Strikingly, Wix and Durable run $6 to $12 more a month.


Once the site needs changes every week, the plan may not be your biggest bill. Whether you pay for those changes[hourly or by subscription](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/subscription-vs-hourly-freelance-cost-analysis) moves your monthly total far more than a $1 gap between two builders.

Four more 10Web alternatives advertise prices below 10Web's. Hostinger, IONOS and ZipWP renew higher after the first term. GoDaddy Airo's Starter is a cent under 10Web on both bases, but like 10Web it publishes no renewal price, and we didn't rank a tool on a one-cent gap.

ZipWP deserves a closer look if you want to stay with AI plus WordPress, because, like 10Web, it builds WordPress sites with AI. Its renewal is still $29 a year above 10Web's prepaid price, and 10Web doesn't publish its own renewal either, so compare the two in writing.


GoDaddy Airo's free plan includes 50 AI credits a month, but its Free card lists no publishing while Starter's reads "Publish 1 site," so we couldn't count it under test (a). Hostinger and GoDaddy Airo still earn places in our[website builders](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/website-builders) ranking, which judges first sites and selling plans rather than price against 10Web.


## 10Web AI alternatives: who does the building


At 10Web, the agents do the building and you finish the site in its editor. The builders on this list put AI in other places:


- WordPress.com and SITE123 draft the site from a chat.
- Framer describes its AI as a design agent.
- Durable's Blog Writer agent keeps posting after launch, 10 posts a month on Launch.
- Strikingly's AI site builder and Jimdo's "website built with AI" produce the first version for you.


A fair test of 10Web AI alternatives is one short brief, the same for each tool, sent to two or three of them. Judge the version you get after asking for changes, and check what AI use costs once the free credits end, such as the 500 trial credits on Framer's free plan.


A prompt gets you a draft in minutes. Choosing what the homepage says first and cutting what visitors skip is still a person's call, which is why we don't expect AI to[replace graphic designers](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/will-ai-replace-graphic-designers) any time soon.


## What staying on WordPress means


WordPress is everywhere, which is part of 10Web's appeal.[W3Techs](https://w3techs.com/technologies/overview/content_management) reports that WordPress runs 40.3% of all websites, a 58.8% share of the sites that use a content management system.


That reach has a cost in upkeep.[Patchstack](https://patchstack.com/whitepaper/state-of-wordpress-security-in-2026/) , a WordPress security company, counted 11,334 new vulnerabilities in the WordPress ecosystem in 2025, a 42% increase on 2024. That ecosystem includes every plugin you'd install on 10Web or WordPress.com, so check who maintains each one before you add it.


One commenter[on Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/vibecoding/comments/1naglvb/help_to_find_the_best_ai_website_builder_for_fast/) put the trade this way: "10Web is solid too, especially if you're okay living in WordPress land, but that also means more things to maintain later." That's one person's experience, not a survey.


If you stay on WordPress and nobody in-house wants that upkeep,[WordPress design agencies](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/wordpress-design-agencies) take on themes, plugins and updates for a fee.


## How hard is it to leave 10Web?


The effort depends on whether your next builder runs WordPress. Move first if you're still on 10Web's 7-day trial, since its help center says a trial site that isn't upgraded gets deleted.


### Moving to WordPress.com


Both platforms run WordPress, so the move goes through the standard WordPress export and import tools. Before you cancel, pick the WordPress.com paid plan you'll move to, since that's where it lists plugins, and confirm each plugin your site needs is available.


### Rebuilding on a builder that isn't WordPress


Plan to rebuild the pages on any builder that doesn't run WordPress, Framer included, unless its own docs offer an import. A rebuild goes more smoothly in this order:


1. Save the text and images from all your 10Web pages while the account is still active.
2. List the plugins and WooCommerce features the site depends on, and confirm the new builder covers each one.
3. Rebuild the homepage on the new builder's free plan and compare it with the original.
4. Move the remaining pages, then connect your domain to the new site.
5. Cancel 10Web a few days before the next billing cycle: its help center says card payments process daily at 12:00 UTC, and its terms say renewals happen "without notifications to you."


A rebuild is also a chance to fix a structure that has grown messy, and[website redesign services](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/website-redesign-services) can take the whole job off your plate.


## How to choose the right 10Web alternative


Match the tool to the reason you're leaving, then check the paid price you'll face in year two:


- To keep WordPress and plugins for less, pick WordPress.com and budget up to $10 a month from year two.
- To avoid a prepay and get a design-led site, start Framer's free plan and move to Basic at $15 month to month.
- To pay nothing for as long as possible, use Jimdo, SITE123, Strikingly, Wix or Durable and accept their subdomains.
- To sell one product without a paid plan, start with Strikingly and budget for its 5% fee.


If your 10Web site runs a WooCommerce store, the builder is the smaller decision. Product pages and checkout decide whether people buy, and that's the work[ecommerce design specialists](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/ecommerce-website-design-companies) are hired for.


## Which 10Web alternative to try first


Pick the test that matters to you and try one tool on one page this week. To keep WordPress, rebuild a page on WordPress.com's free plan; to stop paying altogether, put your homepage on Jimdo's or SITE123's free plan and see whether the free address is good enough.


If you'd rather describe the site and have a person catch what the agents miss, try Awesomic Studio's $20-a-month Basic plan.[Get started](https://www.awesomic.com/studio/pricing) with a single page.


## FAQ


### What are the best alternatives of 10Web on a budget?


WordPress.com and Framer pass both of our cost tests. WordPress.com's Personal plan is $9 month to month, or $4 a month for the first year billed yearly, and Framer Basic costs $15 monthly, or $10 a month if you take the yearly plan. If you'd rather pay nothing, Jimdo, SITE123, Strikingly, Wix and Durable all keep a free site live on a subdomain.


### Does 10Web have a free plan?


Not one that keeps a site live. You can generate a site through "Get started for free," but editing it fully means attaching a credit card to a 7-day Pro trial, and the help center warns that a site nobody upgrades is deleted once the trial expires. AI Starter, the cheapest paid plan, is $20 month to month or $120 for a prepaid year.


### Does 10Web offer refunds?


10Web's own pages disagree: the pricing page advertises a "30-day money back guarantee," and a help-center article states "10Web does not offer refunds." Get an answer from 10Web in writing before you pay, and keep in mind that its terms say subscriptions renew automatically without telling you first.


### Can I move a 10Web site to another builder?


To WordPress.com, yes, through the usual WordPress export and import, since both run WordPress. To Framer or any other builder that doesn't run WordPress, plan to rebuild the pages unless its docs offer an import. If your team can't spare the time, you can hire[an AI website designer](https://www.awesomic.com/hire/hire-an-ai-website-designer) through us for the rebuild.


### Which 10Web alternatives renew at a higher price?


Hostinger Website Builder charges $2.99 a month for Premium on a 48-month term, then $10.99 a month. IONOS's AI website builder moves Starter to $14 and Plus to $20 after a 1-year term, and ZipWP's $99 Starter renews at $149 a year. WordPress.com Personal rises to $8 or $10 a month in its second year, up from $4, at or under 10Web's prepaid rate.
